name: Cobalt and Red Dragons
reason: Combined mention of two separately tracked entities: the Cobalt Dragon (canonical localization of source 'Qinglong') and the Red Dragon coiled together on Zane's soulforge. The paired phrase is covered by the individual entities and is not its own entity.

name: Holy Tree
reason: The source's own English term 'Holy Tree' (the sacred tree with its Hall of the Holy Tree in the Sky Feather Holy Grounds) was retained unchanged in the adaptation.
description: A sacred tree venerated as the heart of a holy ground on the Sea God Continent; its Holy Tree Hall is where Zane shattered the statue of the Queen of Punishment, matching the source's Hall of the Holy Tree in the Sky Feather Holy Grounds. Lavender's soul fragment was later nourished by the Holy Tree in the Sacred Feather Sea.

name: Writhing Weeds
reason: Descriptive English name coined for the source's unnamed mass of wildly growing weeds (spawned by the Resentful Soul Beast in the Jade Emperor Secret Realm chapters), fitting the Western fantasy register.
description: A mass of demonically animated weeds in the secret-realm arc (Eps 844-845) that moves with terrifying speed, burying a warrior under layer after layer of writhing earth. It corresponds to the weeds that suddenly grow wild around the Resentful Soul Beast in the aligned source chapters.

name: Ghost Beads
reason: Source term 'Spiritual Beads' was localized as 'Ghost Beads' for the Western fantasy setting; the Ep 845 line about splitting them evenly directly mirrors the source line about sharing Spiritual Beads equally.
description: Treasure beads harvested in the secret-realm arc (Eps 844-845); fighters agree to split whatever Ghost Beads they obtain evenly, matching the source's Spiritual Beads loot-sharing scene.

name: Eye of Jaylen
reason: The source treasure 'Stone Fire' - a rare mine-found stone used to refine Divine Weapons and worth five Upper Grade Sacred Weapons - was localized as the 'Eye of Jaylen', with added lore naming it after the craftsman Jaylen who forged the four kingdoms' first true divine weapon from one.
description: An extraordinarily precious stone pulled from the mine in the four-kingdoms arc, indestructible by blade or flame and prized above all by weapon smiths (Ep 849). The adaptation names it for the craftsman Jaylen; Fiona refuses it as too precious, and Zane tucks it into his Storage Ring.

name: Great Era
reason: The source's English term 'Great Era' was retained unchanged in the adaptation.
description: A destined age whose descent explains the unprecedented explosion of god-grade geniuses across the four kingdoms (Ep 885); it matches the source's talk of the descended Great Era and the Battle of the Great Era tied to Luo Zheng's fate.

name: Victor Shaw
issues: Surname collision: 'Shaw' is also used for the unrelated Liam Shaw and Yolande Shaw; Victor Shaw is a separate ancient Dragon-blooded figure, not a member of that family.
reason: A full US-style name was assigned to the ancient Dragon-blooded warrior whose preserved corpse features in the secret-realm corpse-possession arc; 'Victor' evokes his standing as the mightiest of his clan.
description: An ancient warrior described as the most powerful of the Dragon-blooded, born with divine strength and retaining a domineering aura even in death (Eps 896-911). His coffin-preserved corpse is inhabited first by War King Wind and later by Zane himself, matching the source arc (~Ch 878-890) in which experts occupy Dragon Bloodline corpses to withstand the Blood Sacrifice Power; his specific source name is not evidenced.

name: Reuben
reason: A US-style given name was assigned to one of the minor source fighters of the Tower of Sin / Sea God Continent arc.
description: A minor fighter who, alongside Lamar and Aldous, recognizes the power behind Zane Lowell's arrows, begs for mercy and then turns on him in the same instant (Eps 945-947). He plausibly corresponds to one of the minor source warriors active in the aligned chapters (the Ha Peng / Yu Ze / Qing Feng group), though no one-to-one match is confirmed.

name: Southern Sky Region
reason: Descriptive Western-style region name used for the sword-filled sky territory; the underlying scene is adapted from the source, but the region's source name is not evidenced.
description: A region whose sky is filled with a sea of hundreds of thousands of great swords, through which a grand jeweled skyship plunges as the swords fall (Eps 964-965). The scene adapts the source chapters (~Ch 943-944) in which Xi Youqin commands millions of giant swords in the sky and sends them crashing down.

name: Alright
reason: Dialogue interjection appearing at sentence starts across 65 episodes; not an entity.

name: Hawkins
issues: Name collision: in Ep 100 'Hawkins' is one of the Seven Great Houses bidding at the Capital auction, while the master sheet separately lists 'Lady Hawkins', Master of Ninety-Foot Peak (Ep 239) - two different referents sharing the surname.
reason: A US-style house surname was assigned to one of the source's seven great noble families of the capital.
description: One of the Seven Great Houses of the Capital; an elder of House Hawkins bids aggressively against House Sutton for the Celestial Essence at the auction (Ep 100), paralleling the source's great-clan bidding war at the Tianlu Auction House.

name: Golden Prairie Diner
reason: Likely a localization of the source's ornate 'Golden Breeze Drizzle Building' in the capital, recast as a Western-style diner; the 'Golden' element and the aligned chapter window support the match, but the evidence is thin.
description: An eatery in the Capital where Zane and two companions share a meal before heading back (Eps 102-103).

name: Crystal Cubes Zane
reason: Extraction artifact: the canonical currency 'Crystal Cubes' run together with the following word 'Zane' across a sentence boundary; not an entity.

name: Quentin
reason: 'Quentin' was assigned as a US-style name for a minor disciple on the Sky Forest mission.
description: A minor scout on the Sky Forest mission who orders two pledges to start a fire at camp (Ep 111); he plausibly localizes one of the minor sect disciples in the source's Cang Qiong (Sky) Forest trial chapters, but no specific counterpart is evidenced.

name: Outer Disciple of Misty Peak
reason: Generic role descriptor ('an outer disciple of Misty Peak'), not a distinct entity; the location Misty Peak is already tracked separately per the master sheet.

name: Lightspeed Slash
reason: Western-style technique name used for a disciple's signature sword art in the source's demon-general battle; no specific source technique name is evidenced.
description: A sword technique Cliff spent years perfecting, empowered by pouring bright silver Life Force into the blade; the demon general disregards it entirely while recoiling from Zane's Shattered Dagger (Ep 113).

name: Grim Reaper
reason: Figurative reference ('his blood-drenched figure evoking the visage of the Grim Reaper himself'), a common metaphor rather than a story entity.

name: Healing Potion
reason: Generic Western fantasy item name standing in for the source's healing pills and medicines.
description: A common restorative consumable; Payne offers one to Zane as the least he could do to make amends (Ep 114).

name: Needle Storm
reason: The source technique 'Pearflower Storm Needles' (used by Zhu Qianning, localized as Ingrid of the Blackwood Clan) was shortened and localized as 'Needle Storm'.
description: Ingrid's signature projectile technique, a lethal storm of needles belonging to the Blackwood Clan's arsenal; to her surprise it fails completely against Zane in the Sky Forest arc (Eps 114-115), matching the Pearflower Storm Needles scene in the source.

name: Detection Needle
reason: The Blackwood Clan's source tool, the Family Zhu's 'Demon Breaking Needle' that captures subtle demon aura, was localized as the 'Detection Needle'.
description: A Blackwood Clan instrument carried by Ingrid that turns from green to red when it senses the faint evil aura a demon gives off even in a victim's form (Ep 115); it matches the Family Zhu's demon-aura-sensing needle described in the source.

name: Infernal Six
reason: The adaptation coined the collective name 'The Infernal Six' for the band of six demon generals that the source depicts without a group name.
description: The six demon generals that corner Zane in a Sky Forest clearing; outnumbered far beyond what he can handle, he unleashes his Nether Essence and kills every last one of them before collapsing (Eps 119-123).

name: Ancient Cauldron
reason: The source's ancient copper/bronze cauldron bearing nine dragon reliefs (including the Azure Dragon relief, localized as the Cobalt Dragon) was localized as the 'Ancient Cauldron'; the show also uses an Ancient Cauldron's thousand-pound weight as a strength benchmark, echoing the source's 'cauldrons of strength' unit.
description: A massive ancient vessel decorated with nine dragons, all eyes closed except the Cobalt Dragon's; Zane watches black flame carry molten iron to the Cobalt Dragon etched on its wall (Eps 12-24). It adapts the source's rampaging copper cauldron and its Azure Dragon relief whose scales empower Luo Zheng.

name: Near-High Level
reason: Generic grade/rank fragment with a single mention and no context; not a distinct entity.

name: Steel Longsword
reason: Generic weapon term used in the adaptation, notably as a flying mount; no specific source counterpart is evidenced.
description: A mundane sword type that cultivators can ride through the air; Lennie descends standing on a small Steel Longsword (Ep 121).

name: Sky Spire
reason: One of the source's two defensive 'Universe and Kun Pagodas' shielding White Emperor City was localized as the 'Sky Spire'; the heaven-oriented Universe (Qian) Pagoda maps to Sky, its Kun counterpart to Stone.
description: One of two massive defensive towers built to hold back the demon hordes (Eps 122-146); its fall, alongside the Stone Spire, lets the demons strike at Silverspire, matching the source's loss of the Universe and Kun Pagodas before the attack on White Emperor City.

name: Stone Spire
reason: One of the source's two defensive 'Universe and Kun Pagodas' shielding White Emperor City was localized as the 'Stone Spire'; the earth-oriented Kun Pagoda maps to Stone, its Universe (Qian) counterpart to Sky.
description: One of two massive defensive towers built to hold back the demon hordes (Eps 122-146); its fall, alongside the Sky Spire, opens the way for the demons' assault on Silverspire, matching the source's loss of the Universe and Kun Pagodas before the attack on White Emperor City.

name: Mirror of Truth
reason: The source's 'Demon Revealing Mirror' (also rendered 'Demon-revealing Mirror' / 'Divine Reflection Mirror'), which exposes demons hiding in human bodies, was localized as the 'Mirror of Truth'.
description: A large mirror used by the city garrison to detect demons concealed in human form (Eps 122-144); it adapts the Demon Revealing Mirror mounted on White Emperor City's walls, which captures subtle demon aura much like the Blackwood Clan's Detection Needle.

name: Healing Needles
reason: Generic Western name for the acupuncture-style medical needles used in the adaptation; no specific source term is evidenced.
description: Therapeutic needles placed on an injured patient's body; Payne works around the Healing Needles already set in Zane's neck while examining him (Ep 123).

name: Zane's Nether Essence
reason: Possessive fragment of the energy 'Nether Essence'; the underlying entity is Nether Essence itself, so this surface form is not a separate entity.

name: Hardening Shards
reason: Western-style name for the cultivation resource allotted by the Lowell household; the source's equivalent training-resource term is not evidenced.
description: A body-tempering resource rationed out by House Lowell: winning the Fatal Duel on Family Training Day doubles a scion's yearly allotment of Hardening Shards (Ep 13), and disciples collect their allotment at Misty Peak (Ep 95).

name: Stamina Pill
reason: Generic Western fantasy pill name standing in for the source's common cultivation pills.
description: A common consumable pill that restores a warrior's energy; offered as a duel bonus on Family Training Day (Ep 13) and fumbled for mid-brawl by a fighter (Ep 33).

name: Rainbow Gown
reason: Descriptive Western name for Yolande Shaw's (source Yun Luo's) elaborate garment; the source's name for the gown is not evidenced.
description: Yolande Shaw's elaborate garment, fastened with intricate knots, which she begins untying without warning to Zane's alarm (Ep 130); listed in the master sheet as her signature equipment.

name: Sky and Stone Spires
reason: Combined mention of the two separately tracked towers, the Sky Spire and the Stone Spire (source 'Universe and Kun Pagodas'); the paired phrase is not its own entity.

name: Glass Ward
reason: Western-style name for the transparent containment barrier in the Sacred Flame arc; the source's term for the confinement is not evidenced.
description: A transparent containment barrier that leaves Zane immobilized and utterly vulnerable, unable even to turn his head (Eps 133-134); it corresponds to his confinement during the Sacred Flame events adapted from the source's Sky Demon Sacred Fire chapters (~Ch 121-123).

name: Archfiends
reason: The elite demonic commanders of the siege arc (the source's Demon Kings / Beast Kings fought at White Emperor City) appear to have been localized as 'Archfiends', though the mapping is only weakly evidenced.
description: Elite demonic beings far above ordinary demon generals, fielded in the great siege battle; one fights on while nursing significant wounds (Ep 136), and by the battle's end two Archfiends are dead alongside the defeated demon (Ep 146).

name: Titan's Pillar
issues: Master sheet describes Titan's Pillar as 'Orion's chain/pillar weapon', but Eps 136-137 depict the Titan's Pillars as spirit-infused pillar snares that bind warriors with chains and are shattered by Axel - the two descriptions conflict and should be reconciled.
reason: Western mythic name ('Titan') given to the massive spirit-pillars of the siege-arc battle; the source's term for them is not evidenced.
description: Massive, seemingly indestructible pillars that snare warriors in chains, choking off their Life Force and dragging them from the sky (Eps 136-137). When Axel's hammer shatters one, it reveals its true nature: an ancient evil spirit forced to dissolve back into The Cosmos.

name: Bloodletter
reason: Evocative Western weapon name given to a veteran warrior's legendary enchanted blade; the source weapon's name is not evidenced.
description: The legendary enchanted blade of a battle-scarred Soul Realm veteran: an ordinary-looking machete that elongates and shimmers when charged with Life Force, a masterwork said to slice through anything it touches (Ep 136).

name: Titan’s Pillar
reason: Same entity as Titan's Pillar; the variant differs only in the curly apostrophe used in some episode files.

name: Godforge Technique
reason: The adaptation coined 'Godforge Technique' for the source's titular body-refining method by which the protagonist forges his own body into a weapon on the path to godhood; the NovelHi translation's exact name for the manual is not evidenced.
description: Zane's foundational cultivation method, introduced as 'The Original Method of Forging: transform flesh into forge, body into weapon. Purify the vessel through suffering' (Ep 4). It underpins his entire path, cultivating his body and Soul Power to tremendous depths (Eps 14, 373), and adapts the source novel's core refining-into-god method that defines Luo Zheng's rise.

name: Ambrosia Pill
reason: The source's 'Seven Treasures Nirvana Elixir', one of the few truly valuable treasures in the Imperial Army's Treasury, was localized as the 'Ambrosia Pill' to fit the Western fantasy register.
description: A rare, miraculous pill Zane selects as his third choice from the treasury rewards (Eps 142-143), matching the source's Seven Treasures Nirvana Elixir, which is usable only by practitioners below the Divine Reflection Realm.

name: Sequoia Circle
reason: The source's 'Bamboo Leaf Gang' (also rendered 'Bamboo Forest Gang'), the bandit band headquartered in Jade Dragon Valley, was localized as the 'Sequoia Circle', swapping the bamboo motif for a Western tree.
description: A bandit gang whose base camp lies in Dragon Valley, littered with weapons, whiskey barrels and crude cabins (Eps 146-147). Its members fear the Seven Ruling Families, who could wipe out the Sequoia Circle without breaking a sweat - directly matching the source's Bamboo Leaf Gang of Jade Dragon Valley and the seven noble families.
